package_info.why_malicious: The package is designed to steal Discord user tokens and browser information from multiple browsers and exfiltrate this data to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook. It masquerades as a legitimate module, uses typosquatting, and executes malicious code at install and runtime.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code executes the main app.js file, which initiates the malicious data collection and exfiltration process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running arbitrary code at install time is a common malware technique to ensure execution even if the package is never explicitly imported.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute code on install except for legitimate build or setup tasks; here, it is used to trigger data theft.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall for build steps or dependency checks, but not for user data access.
key_indicators: no legitimate build or setup task

execution_context.file_location: app.js and classes/Grabber.js, Token.js, User.js, Util.js

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code scans browser and Discord directories for LevelDB files, extracts Discord tokens and browser data, collects system and user information, and retrieves the public IP address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing browser and Discord data directories to extract tokens and user information is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access LevelDB files in browser or Discord directories, nor do they collect user tokens or system information.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensics or backup tools may access such data with user consent, but not in a package claiming to be a Discord utility.
key_indicators: Extraction of tokens and user/system info
Use of public IP lookup service

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After collecting data, the code sends the stolen tokens and user information to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive data to an external webhook is a hallmark of information-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not send user tokens or browser data to external servers, especially not via Discord webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Webhooks are used for legitimate notifications, but never for exfiltrating user credentials.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhook for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is executed during package installation via the postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initiates the main malicious logic in app.js.

attack_chain.action: The main script scans browser and Discord directories, extracts tokens and user/system information, and collects the public IP address.
attack_chain.leads_to: Prepares the stolen data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected data is sent to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and user information.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of arbitrary code during npm install (postinstall script)
Access to LevelDB files in browser and Discord directories
Collection of Discord tokens and user/system information
Network requests to Discord webhooks with sensitive data
file_indicators: Presence of postinstall script in package.json
References to browser/Discord data directories in code
network_indicators: Outgoing HTTPS POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/*
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for postinstall scripts that execute main code. Flag any access to LevelDB files in browser or Discord directories. Detect network requests to Discord webhooks, especially those containing tokens or user data. Look for package files or code referencing token grabbing or browser data extraction.
